title: Habio: Where Your Money Checks In But It Never Leaves
body:
If you’re considering downloading Habio, prepare for a journey where your wallet becomes the star of a hostage situation—only, there’s no Liam Neeson coming to save you. I embarked on this misadventure when I downloaded Habio, lured in by its glossy façade and the promise of seamless productivity. Instead, I was greeted by an ensemble of glitches that would make even a beta version blush in embarrassment.

Despite the allure of streamlined interfaces and productivity promises, Habio is less a tool for organization and more a trap for your finances. It’s like buying a first-class ticket on the Titanic purely for the iceberg experience. I attempted to make the best of a sinking situation until the frustration overwhelmed the functionality. When I sought a refund, hoping for some semblance of customer service redemption, I was met with a cold shoulder draped in the fine print of their “terms and conditions.”

The audacity of Habio’s customer service—or should I say, their customer disservice?—is a masterclass in how to alienate users. They hold onto your money with the tenacity of a toddler clutching a favourite toy, making it clear that your financial well-being ranks several leagues below their bottom line.

Let this review serve as a warning: Habio’s real functionality lies in its ability to perform a vanishing act with your cash. Don’t fall for the trap. There are countless other apps and services that actually respect their users and understand the value of customer satisfaction.

title: Do not download this app
body:
Hello, fellow App Store customer.
Read me for some good tea.

I write this review today after a horrendous month of contact with Habio.

I downloaded the app, hopeful and happy. Upon downloading, i realized that it wasn’t really going to help me, so in July 2023, after 1 week, canceled my free trial, I deleted the app, and forgot about it.
I receive a charge (6) months later in February 1st 2024 from habio.
I contact the company, and they respond with “i cancelled too late” - 6 months later? No. I then asked for the specific dates that i allegedly signed up and canceled - with continued emails from them throughout February (6 emails in total) insisting that i had canceled my subscription successfully and would not be further charged, but i was not eligible for a refund.

I suspected this was a scam, since I had not had my phone for 2 months (I am on an island doing scuba training) and i certainly hadn’t had downloaded it again or re subscribed in January or February - simply because i had absolutely no means to.

I submitted a chargeback with my bank after a month, (march 2nd) and on march 5th i got my money back because of my bank <3

I also received an email from habio on march 5th saying that my subscription was NOW cancelled, a month after they said 1) i was already cancelled, and 2) they promised me multiple times in the emails throughout February that i was already cancelled. So, why, pray tell, that I am getting an email on the 5th of march that only NOW my subscription is cancelled?

They want to send out this easy money, and try to make it impossible to get your money back. Stay at them, do not accept no for an answer, and when you have enough evidence, take it to your bank and they will handle the rest for you. Enjoy!

title: Vorsicht Betrug!!!!
body:
Nachdem Sie ein einwöchiges Probeabo am 13.06.24 für 9,99€ abgeschlossen hatten und es dann direkt am 15.06.24 innerhalb der App gekündigt haben (ein Screenshot der Kündigungsbestätigung liegt vor), wurden am 27.06.24 insgesamt 49,99€ abgebucht. 

Auf Nachfrage beim Kundenservice, die mir dann 7 Tage später antwortet, wurde mir mitgeteilt, dass das Geld (also die 49,99€) nicht zurückerstattet werden kann, da ich die Kündigungsfrist nicht eingehalten hätte. Zwei Tage gelten also nicht als fristgerecht? Das verstehe ich absolut nicht und bin echt erstaunt über diese betrügerische Masche! Das Geld wurde von meiner Seite zurückgezogen bzw. als unberechtigt gemeldet. 

Die App ist ausschließlich auf Englisch und auch der Support reagiert ausschließlich auf Englisch. Dies zur Information, da nicht jeder dieser Sprache mächtig ist.

title: Unerwartet gut

Nach langem rumklicken hat die App endlich bei mir klick gemacht. Ich bin nun total begeistert wie Habio mir hilft ruhiger zu werden. Ich konnte mit Spaß mein Morgen organisieren, meine Wohnung in Ordnung bringen. Ich bin dadurch entspannter und sogar besser gelaunt. Mein Frust gegen mich selbst verschwindet. Ich kriege durch Habio die Kontrolle wieder zurück.

Es ist das Geld Wert!

Die an die ich geschrieben habe, stand aber als Mail für Rückfragen und Kündigungen auf der Internetseite. Find das alles echt eine Frechheit! body:

However I could not find any receipt, confirmation email or the items I had allegedly bought anywhere on my account, the app of my email.

To this date they have not refunded me and keep claiming this case is out of their refunding policy.

I was definitely scammed by this app.

title: FRAUD
body: Beware of fraud! This app states that it offers a trial period (3 days for $1). But they book you immediately for $29.99 and 3 days later again for $29.99. They do not allow you to officially cancel any kind of subscription and are fraudulently listed in the App Store for one-time purchases - but they are a subscription that cannot be canceled. So you can not manage subscriptions via App Store or in your Subscriptions area. No one responds to customer service emails. There is only one automatic email every day that takes up to 4 days to process the request. But there is no real answer. They make it impossible to cancel!!!

title: Warning: SCAM ALERT!
body:
I recently fell victim to a blatant scam by Habio. Their app is designed to deceive users into making in-app purchases through misleading visuals and fine print. They tricked me into buying a PDF file for 29.99 euros, making it appear as though the product was free. The payment terms were deliberately hidden in a pale layout, ensuring most customers wouldn't notice until it was too late.

This is nothing short of FRAUD. The response from the merchant was dismissive, claiming that I had consented to the purchase. This is a lie. I did not consent to being scammed.

I will not let this slide. As a digital content creator, I am using every platform at my disposal to expose their deceitful practices. I will post reviews on the App Store, Play Store, Facebook, Trustpilot, and every other major review site to warn others.

Furthermore, their actions may be in direct violation of European consumer protection laws, particularly those related to transparent pricing and fair trading. I am prepared to report their practices to the relevant authorities and pursue legal action.

Do not fall for this scam. Avoid Habio at all costs and spread the word about their fraudulent behavior.

P.S: They will now respond to my review with a comment asking me to contact them by email, I did, and they will pretend to be professional and all, don't fall for that.

title: 🚨Arnaque🚨 Lisez entièrement ça vous évitera de vous faire avoir 🚨
body:
Attention cette application est une arnaque.

Premièrement on vient vous hameçonner en français alors qu’une fois l’abonnement souscrit tout est en anglais.

Mais ça ne est rien à côté de des paiements frauduleux qu’ils se permettent de faire.

J’ai souscris à l’essaie de 14 jours, soit 9,99€

Et à la suite de ça on voit propose un ebook en pdf, et si vous avez le malheur de cliquer dessus (chose que j’ai fait 2 x) et bien vous serez prélevé sans demande de confirmation de paiement (car lors de la souscription à l’abonnement la vérification est demandé donc ils ne la redemande pas ensuite). Leur système est vraiment bien ficelé.

J’ai reçu aussi un mail me confirmant mon paiement de 9.99€ avec une mention qui précise que je serai débité de 49.99€ dans 14 jours.

C’est une honte qu’une telle application existe sur l’Apple Store.

J’espère réussir à bloquer les paiements et me faire rembourser par l’assurance de ma banque. Car cette application ne rembourse visiblement rien de ce que j’ai pu lire sur des sites d’avis.

Ps: ne m’envoyez pas votre message automatique je vous ai déjà écris plusieurs mails.

title: Arnaque
body:
Même après avoir annulé l’essai ils vous débitent sur votre carte bancaire car l’abonnement est géré en dehors de l’appstore. 
Une fois dans l’app : Ils vous proposent un essai à moins de 1€ pour ensuite pouvoir débiter votre carte quand ils veulent. 
Des vrais rapaces qui profitent de personnes en situation de vulnérabilité avec des annonces accrocheuses du style “la solution pour améliorer le quotidien des personnes TDAH” (en anglais ADHD) 
Alors qu’en fait ils se servent ensuite sur votre compte en sachant pertinemment à quel point le TDAH est difficile à vivre au quotidien notamment vis à vis de la gestion financière.
Ils se frottent les mains en se disant « super je vais pouvoir me servir sur leurs comptes et ils ne vont pas s’en apercevoir, étant donné qu’ils ont des difficultés dans la gestion de leurs argent et ne vont pas nécessairement vérifier leurs comptes tout les jours. » 
De vrai voleurs qui profitent du fait que les personnes atteintes de TDAH comme moi essayent de s’améliorer et cherchent un moyen de s’en sortir. 
Les personnes qui ont monté cette arnaque devraient avoir honte !

title: Do not get this app!
body:
After following an ad on Instagram targeted at helping someone with ADHD improve their habits and routines I decided to give Habio a go and signed up for a 3-day for €5.49. €5.49 seemed like a reasonable amount to see if the app could fulfil on the promises made in the advertising and offer.

However, after the trial offer was accepted, a screen with a large brightly coloured button saying ‘Get my PDF workbook’ appears. As someone with ADHD, I made the mistake of impulsively clicking on the button without stopping to read the surrounding text.

I immediately realised my mistake when I was taken to a screen that told me I had been charged an extra $29.99 for the ebook. Because my intention was only to go for the trial to test the app, not purchase a $29.99 ebook (which I would most likely never read) I didn’t click on the link to download the ebook and got in touch with the Habio helpdesk to explain my mistake and ask for a refund.

I thought it was a reasonable request, especially as I had contacted them the moment I realised my mistake and, more importantly, hadn’t given my consent for the extra charge. At least that’s what I thought. 

Upon contacting the Habio support I was told there was a strict no refund policy and that I had given my permission via the terms and conditions and that all the information was readily available on the PDF purchase screen. After they provided screenshots of the offer pages it became clear that this offer is only designed to trick someone into clicking on the more expensive upsell PDF button.

On review of the ‘Special Offer’ screen, all the important information, such as price and consent to the extra charge, are in a type size and colour designed to blend with the background, making it almost illegible on a quick scan of the page. The consent to charge text is in such a low contrast colour with the background, and such a tiny type size that it hurts my eyes to even read it!

It feels as though this page has been designed with the intent of tricking the very type of person that they claim to want to help into making a purchase that on quick glance would appear to be a PDF attached to the trial offer you’ve agreed to, without clear extra charge.

Very disappointed that there are companies out there like Habio trying to take advantage of underhanded sales tactics rather than genuinely wanting to help and make a positive difference in the world.

title: Disappointing, slow response time and misleading.
body:
I signed up for this app for a number of reasons, but was particularly taken in by the different style of reading that would help me with reading quicker, as advertised on social media. I liked the idea of the positivity and enforcing helpful routines. 
I signed up for a week’s trial (which I was disappointed I’d have to pay for, but went along with it). I understood this was an isolated transaction and if I wanted to continue, I would have the choice after I’d finished the trial. 
After my initial look through the app, I couldn’t find anything on the reading, and then with work etx, didn’t have chance to commit any time to the app in that week. Which I agree is my fault, but the whole point of the app is to be supportive and enforce positive routines. I accepted that that trial was a waste of my money through my own fault but was disappointed to have been charged approximately £26 when they have continued to charge my card. I haven’t used the app since and each correspondence takes about a week for them to reply. I’ve provided them with my bank statement as proof of the transaction, but they refuse to refund me the money that I don’t recall ever haven given permission for them to take. 
Given the point of this app, and those they’re trying to appeal to, I find them to be misleading and taking advantage when they put themselves across as being a way to improve and support. I haven’t gone back to this app even though I’ve seemingly paid for it, as I’m quite frankly angry at how they conduct business.

title: Waste of £30
body:
Firstly this app doesn’t offer a free trial so you have to commit from the outset. I opted for the best value of £27.99 for the year as the app and the reviews seemed good.
It was a downhill slide from there unfortunately.

The app is seriously buggy.
View settings often don’t work and endless tapping to move through screens because it hangs constantly.
There is no option to ‘ignore’ certain features and takes you round and round in loops until you select something that you never wanted in the first place. For instance I want to record a habit but don’t necessarily want to log one of their options for reward such as listen to a song or eat a piece of fruit (seriously who devised these?) but it will prompt you to death until you go through the motions.

With the habit tracking itself I’d like the option to say I’d like to do something x-times a week. The set up on this is you have to say which days you’ll do it. Thanks, but life doesn’t always work like that and I’d just like to know that I achieved my commitment of number of days.

The journal is yet another prompt based system so pre-defined responses with some free text but not very intuitive. Want to include a photo in your journal?  Nope sorry that feature doesn’t exist.
Want to see your achievements in calendar view? No sorry can’t do that either.

Want to log in on your iPad? You can but only once you’ve worked through the entire initial set up process all over again. Seriously developers just add a log in option at the beginning!!

There are some nice articles and short reads on wellbeing topics included which is the best part of this app but not necessarily what people are coming here for.  If this is what you were coming here for I’d suggest you save yourself the cash and take a look at the wellbeing section on apple news.

I’ve already cancelled the subscription so I don’t forget and it renews in a years time, but I’m beyond disappointed with the usability of the app and endless prompts that extend into being seriously irritating.

If you’re a person incapable of thinking for yourself then this is probably for you. For everyone else you’ll feel like you’re being treated like an idiot and irritated by needless and unwanted options that you didn’t ask for.

title: Unfair refund policy
body:
I recently had an unfortunate experience with the Habio app's refund policy, which left me quite disappointed. I was charged $49.99 for a subscription that I didn't knowingly sign up for. When I contacted customer support with proof of the unintended transaction, I was met with a response that did not address my concerns adequately.

The customer support representative informed me that I had apparently registered for the subscription and pointed me to their Money-Back Policy and Billing Terms. While I understand the importance of clear terms and conditions, I believe that businesses should also consider cases where customers genuinely find themselves in unwanted subscriptions. In my situation, I had not even utilized the app's services.

Despite my plea for a refund, the response essentially stated that the charge could not be reversed. This lack of flexibility in addressing customer concerns is disheartening, especially when I hadn't received any value from the subscription.

I strongly urge the Habio app team to reconsider their refund policy and make it more customer-centric. Transparency and fairness are key to maintaining trust with users. This experience has left me with a negative impression of the app's customer service and policies. As a result, I can't recommend the app to others in good faith.

I hope my review can contribute to positive changes and encourage the company to prioritize customer satisfaction in situations like these.

title: “ work books cost 29.99 euro” I charged 60.99 euro
body: I recently encountered a disappointing experience with the Habio app. After discovering the app through an advertisement on Instagram, I decided to explore it by taking advantage of their 1 euro trial offer. My intent was to evaluate the app as a potential tool for my students to build better habit routines. However, within minutes of signing up, I was unexpectedly charged 69.99 euros. Upon contacting customer support, I learned that this charge was for downloading two PDFs within the app. To my surprise, the cost breakdown suggested that each PDF, with only about 30 pages, was valued at nearly 30 euros—essentially charging 1 euro per page. This pricing seems excessively high for what is provided, especially when considering that it was not clearly communicated upfront. As someone who frequently tests educational tools and apps, I find this pricing structure unreasonable and not justifiable. If books or resources for building habits were priced this way, they would be inaccessible to many. Unfortunately, this experience has left me with a negative impression of Habio, and I cannot recommend it to others, especially those who are mindful of their budgets.

title: 사기 scam
body:
시험사용기간 3일에 1불 결제를 유도한 뒤, 승인되면 추가 결제 29.99불은 사용자의 추가 인증이 필요치 않는점을 악용한 사기어플. 이미 피해를 보신분들은 카드사나 페이팔에 직접 연락하세요. 개발사는 이 글에도 도와줄테니 연락하라고 복붙 하겠지만 이메일 보내봐야 응답 제대로 안함. 다들 애플 앱스토어에 ‘사기 신고‘ 한번씩 넣으세요.
(업데이트) 페이팔에 사기신고 넣었더니 환불받았습니다. 
———
 This is a scam app that entices a $1 charge for a 3-day trial period and then exploits the fact that no additional authentication is needed from the user for an additional charge of $29.99 once approved. At the registration stage, a button to download the report is intentionally displayed after completing a survey. It leads users to think that the report is about the survey and prompts them to download it. As soon as they do, an additional charge of $29.99 is made. If the auto-payment option is not unchecked, there is a risk of being double-charged. If you have already been a victim, please contact your credit card company or PayPal directly. The developer might say in this post that they will help, so contact them, but sending an email is usually futile as they seldom respond properly. Everyone, please file a ‘scam report’ on the Apple App Store.

title: 29.9달러를 도둑맞고 싶으시면 설치하세요!
body: 피해자가 더는 없길 바라며 리뷰를 남깁니다. 요약하면 평가판 취소가 실패해도 환불을 안해주는 강도들은 처음 봅니다. 그냥 사용하지 않으시길 권장드립니다. 평가판을 사용하고 삭제하려고 했는데 이메일로 확인을 요청했습니다. 이메일에서 확인을 하니 뭔가 잘못되었다면서 환불이 성공적으로 진행이 되지 않았습니다. 결제가 안된건가, 다른 이메일로 가입했나 싶어서 결제 내역도 찾아봤으나 다른 환불 방법을 도저히 찾을 수가 없었습니다. 앱 내에서 환불도 안되고 결제 내역에도 환불 안내도 없고요. 바쁜 시간 쪼갰는데 환불이 안되니 아주 화가 나더라고요. 며칠 후에 29.9달러가 결제되었습니다. 고객 센터에 연락했더니 환불 정책에 맞지 않는다고 해서 환불을 거절 당했습니다. 환불을 시도한 이메일과 문제 상황을 꼼꼼히 설명했는데도 불구하고 말이죠. 더 화가 났습니다. 저는 UX 디자인 쪽에서 일하는 사람입니다. 환불을 어렵게 만드는 전형적인 다크 패턴이 있는 앱인 건 참았는데 환불도 안될 줄은 몰랐습니다. 이런 쓰레기 같은 앱과 정책이 있는 서비스는 망해야 한다고 생각하여 공익적인 목적으로 글을 남깁니다. 읽어주셔서 감사합니다.

title: Abusive Terms - No refund - Paid Trial - No right of withdrawal
body:
If I could give less than 1 star, I would.  ABUSIVE billing terms. 

You pay 29,90 Euros for one month of subscription, and according to their terms/conditions, you have no right to a refund, even if you cancel within the trial period, they must be notified, at least, 24hours before the trial expires. Factually their 3 days trial for 1,00 Euro is actually a 2 two days trial, that will cost you much more than what they advertise. 

EU residents: They undermine your consumer rights in their “100% money policy guarantee policy” by revoking your right to withdraw within 14 days as dictated under EU law. 

Do not install this app, that’s the best advice I can give. Their support staff is unhelpful and take days to answer one single email.

body: I wouldn’t recommend this app. I logged in on a browser and chose the 24 day trial for 12.99 to see if I liked the app and if it helped with my adhd related planning and organisation issues. Then received an email thanking me for my $100 payment as I hadn’t cancelled during the trial period. I couldn’t find it under my subscriptions to cancel anywhere. When I contacted them about it and asked them to refund my payment, they refused as the situation didn’t meet the criteria in their refund policy. I explained the situation, and that I wasn’t able to access the premium features in the app, and that I wasn’t interested in continuing, but they only responded that I wasn’t eligible under their refund policy. I would suggest their business model is more based off being sneaky and relying on fine print and poorly communicated payments than on actually helping people with organisation and planning. A truly massive disappointment.

title: Beware of putting your money on the table!
body: Though I cannot judge a company's service or product, I will share my less then positive experience with setting up the app. I am not stating that any of this is made by design (but I have my doubts). When you set up the app it asks for $1 for 3 days trial which is not much money, and the user leaves their credit card information. Then, once you're in, you're presented with a supporting PDF document. However, beware of clicking anywhere because there's no purchase page. Rather, the purchase is automatically completed and you're charged $27. Then, if you complain, they say they've thoroughly reviewd your purchase and you're not eligible for refund as you're request isn't compliant with their refund policy. Additionally, they take 3-4 business days to respond to your message, reassuring you all the way that they're busy, only to charge you additional $27 for a monthly subscription even though you've unsubscribed. When you complain, they answer you within 1 minute to tell you the same thing - we are not giving you YOUR money back. All of it is perfectly crafted and hidden in the plain sight under the "by continuing you agree to everything we set up in our little sheme". And just to mention, all of this happens before you have even downloaded or registered with your email for the app service. So, I resepect the work they've put into their product and service, but beware where you click and how you interact with this company because they've put some thought into convenient and easy use (read: parting you with your money before you even have a chance to see what you've signed up for).

Despite my attempts to cancel before the trial ended, their customer support was unresponsive for over 2 weeks, resulting in my card being automatically charged when trial period ends. When requesting a refund, they claimed the payment was authorised, ignoring the attempts to contact them. This is an unethical practice and I urge whoever reading to not download this app.
author: Kloe8284

title: Beware of Unethical Practices - Stay away from Habio
body: One of the most glaring issues is the lack of transparency regarding their subscription and billing processes. I have only signed up for their one week trial and since then the app has been charging me monthly. There’s no straightforward method provided for users to unsubscribe, and it doesn’t show up in your Apple App Store as subscription. It’s evident that Habio is more interested in taking your money than providing a user-friendly experience. I’m very disappointed with this experience. I urge the team to look into this issue as soon as possible.

title: Another Fraudulent Charge Complaint
body:
I’m another person who had the rug pulled out from under them with their billing practices. I signed up for a 14-Day free trial and about three days in found it wasn’t for me. Upon sign up, you’re told that you’ll receive a reminder email before your trial is up that you’ll be moved to a paid subscription. The day before my trial ended, they took the money and THEN emailed me and said my trial was up the following day. I wrote support and asked for my money back for the reasons I detailed here. They responded six days later telling me my subscription was cancelled (which I had already done at this point) and that I won’t be charged anymore. I responded and thanked them for that and inquired about the refund and no response. This was going on three weeks ago. I encourage folks who have had a similar experience to let the Better Business Bureau, the FTC, and econsumer dot gov know. No matter the efficacy of an app like this, taking money from people actively trying to improve their capacity for executive function is incredibly sinister. It’s preying on the very thing people using this app are seeking help with.

EDIT: I’ve been told that their Money-Back Policy does not cover my request…

title: This app is a sham.
body:
I describe this app as a sham instead of a scam since I am sure they have found a  loophole to continue operating legally. 

That said,  I bought a two week trial for $9.99 assuming I could cancel at anytime due to their cancellation policy and money back guarantee. 

After purchasing the app, I realized I could not use/explore the app due to an (optional) $30 workbook that helps complete the daily routine/exercises. I really don’t remember reading about any “necessary” materials, so I immediately cancelled with no issue by using the app. 

Unfortunately, when I asked for my money back, customer service explained the guarantee did not apply to trial memberships. When I emailed back asking for the “money back guarantee” language/fine print, I began receiving automated emails that customer service could not answer emails from the same address I had just messaged them so they forwarded me another email address to reach them. An address that comes back returned,  or no one responds when you email.  It’s my opinion they are hoping people will stop pursuing their refund due to no response.  At $10 a pop I’m sure they are making bank. 

With that, they have underestimated this highly principled Karen with nothing to do but message their customer service and litter the internet with complaints. 

This app needs to go.

title: Save yourself the money and Read the detailed reviews
body:
Their marketing is unprecedented. My ADHD brain was sucked in fast and thought wow this is the solution to all of my problems! 
Nope it's just one more app to clutter my phone. All of the "routines" are premade. It makes zero sense. What if I want the routine to include a workout but not meditation? Too bad, you have about a handful of options and you have to get lucky that they meet your exact needs. There's no learning or changing the brain or making your day easier. 
Write down your own routine and set an alarm. You'll achieve a much better outcome on your own rather than wasting $25 a month. Which is crazy expensive for getting a bunch of mediocre info and premade lists that likely aren't going to match any person precisely. Also they refuse to give refunds if the app doesn't meet your expectations. That should be the biggest red flag.

author: Jerel85

title: Dark patterns galore- don’t sign up
body:
This app is a scam and should be removed from the App Store / banned from social media advertising. I wish I had seen the other reviews before signing up for a $10 2 week trial. 

As soon as I saw the litany of complaints about fraudulent billing and difficulties canceling subscriptions, I immediately submitted a cancelation request through the app and emailed their CS team. While the app does show you a confirmation screen upon submitting your cancelation request, the app itself does not update to show a static message about your canceled status. title: This is a Scam - Do NOT download this app
body:
Do NOT download this app, they will scam you. My experience with Habio has left me extremely disappointed and frustrated. Despite adhering to their cancellation policy by promptly canceling my subscription literally within 5 mins of opting into the trial, I was shocked to see that they still charged me for a full month's subscription fee. What’s even more worrisome and shady about this situation is that I never even used the app nor have I filled out anything on the app to further it’s use. When I got an email back from them, they stated verbatim: 

“Our technical support has thoroughly checked your order. We see that on 11 SEP 2023 you've purchased a subscription to our Habio app. Since the subscription has not been canceled, after three days of trial, you've been charged $29.99 for a month of using the app. The payment cannot be unauthorized.” 

I quite literally sent an email to cancel 5 mins after opting in. They did not throughly check this so called “order” and I have NOT used the app at all. 

Do not listen to the developer response either as it’s a shady, poor attempt to mislead you into thinking they’re on top of this and addressing the situation when they are not. They WILL take your money and run. It's disheartening to see a company resort to such dishonest practices, misleading customers with free trials and then failing to honor their own terms and pretend they are helping to service it’s customers. Avoid at all cost.

title: Distracting dashboard
body:
The progress dashboard has this For You section where there’s always a bunch of eye-grabbing attempts to upsell you. Just above that there’s always this bubblehead with some notification or suggestion for you - also in an attempt to upsell you or increase your usage of the app.

This makes landing on the app quite stressful and distracting. I love the look and feel of the app, it’s calming and feels in line with the mindful act of being intentional with one’s habits - or so it would be if the dashboard where you need to record each milestone wasn’t a mini Time Square Billboard showcase.

Ultimately, I find that this makes me far less likely to engage the app - especially when I’ve just hit a pre-bedtime milestone. 

If apps designed to reduce mental clutter, constant advertisements and help position you for sticking to your goals without constant pushing to add to that list of goals matters to you, then you’d best look elsewhere!
